profile.headline: Staff software engineer
profile.summary:
With over 10 years of industry experience working at different levels of the software stack, I have a broad perspective. 

I’ve been tech lead for the home timeline on twitter.com and the backend Tweet service that handles all Tweet reads and writes.

I enjoy writing code, teaching and mentoring other engineers, writing documentation, and designing reliable services.

positions.title: Tech Lead, Tweet Service
positions.description:
For my last year or so at Twitter I was tech lead for the backend Tweet Service, the service responsible for all core Tweet read and write business logic. All real-time serving reads flowed through our service, and our read traffic was measured in tens of millions of Tweets per second. Write traffic was in the tens of thousands of writes per second.

In this role I developed the long-term strategy for the Tweet service, moving towards a model that would enable rapid development of Tweet-based features at scale, which was essential for moving the business forward as Tweets were one of the biggest areas of product development.

Some highlights from this role:

- Mentored ~20 engineers within the team and across the company in various focus areas, such as career development, software design, and Scala
- Communicated and collaborated with cross-functional peers and stakeholders to ensure our projects were solving the right problems
- Designed and shipped an optimization in collaboration with product teams that reduced total Tweet reads by ~5% by avoiding duplicative work

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer, Tweet Service
positions.description:
By 2016 I had been working on various aspects of Twitter's web site for over four years and was looking for a change. I was lucky to find a position on the Tweet Service team. This was my first experience working on highly scalable distributed systems, and really expanded my Scala knowledge. Over time I became an expert in most parts of our software stack.

Some highlights:

- Proposed and led a change to how various Tweet health signals were stored (for example, misinfo, spam, non-ad-safe content, etc.), allowing a ~10x increase in the number of possible signals for Tweets
- Led the Tweet service aspect of various projects, such as the change from 140 to 280 characters and conversation controls (known as Who can reply?)
- Led large-scale refactorings to make our codebase more approachable to engineers new to Scala and functional programming (historically the team was senior and FP-oriented, which was reflected in the code)
- On-call for several core services, including the Tweet service, and various services related to fetching URL data and shortening/expanding URLs in Twitter’s t.co format
- Helped design our Visibility Filtering framework, a patented solution for enabling rapid development of features related to removing, hiding, or downranking content on the platform
- Acted as a “shepherd” in interview huddles for our hiring diversity program, helping teams avoid bias in interviewing

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer, twitter.com
positions.description:
I joined Twitter as a junior front-end engineer at the end of 2011. I was promoted to Senior SWE in 2012 and then to Staff SWE in 2015. I worked on a large number of different teams, focusing on the profile page, Tweet detail, notifications page, and home timeline.

One of my favorite parts of this period was working on a small vertical team comprised of backend timelines engineers, an EM, a PM, a designer, and one engineer from each of the client teams in order to bring threaded conversations to Twitter's home timeline.

One of my biggest contributions during my tenure as a front-end engineer was my organizational work to bring together the disparate web teams to share ideas and form community. At this time, the various teams were fairly isolated due to the org structure, which was organized around product teams. I created two recurring meetings, one for the leads of each team to sync and make sure our technical solutions were working towards a common goal, and one for all the teams to get together socially, and give tech talks.

Some highlights from this role:

- Tech lead for the web home timeline team, responsible for prioritizing and assigning work, communicating with peers and stakeholders
- Generalized common patterns into reusable components in Scala and JavaScript
- Designed and implemented a JavaScript testing tool to facilitate the twitter.com backend move from Ruby to Scala
- Designed and implemented a system for measuring and viewing web performance data

positions.title: Head of Development
positions.description:
I was a jack-of-all-trades at Bookcraft, being heavily involved in all aspects of the company's core business of project management for small and large publishing companies as well as self-publishers, while also building websites and other digital products for our customers, and building a Ruby on Rails project management database for our own use. 

- Project-managed book pre-production for major publishers, handling the process from receiving the author’s manuscript and artwork to creating print-ready PDFs
- Used Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop to lay out books, redraw illustrations in house style, and process artwork to house specifications
- Trained staff in Adobe Creative Suite software
- Created scripts for InDesign for creating barcodes and automating book cover and dust jacket layouts
- Built CMS-backed websites for our customers
- Implemented a custom project management database in Ruby on Rails

patents.title: Messaging System With Capability To Edit Sent Messages (Edit Tweet)
patents.description: This is the patent for our design of the Edit Tweet feature.

patents.title: Visibility Filtering
patents.description: This was the patent for our Visibility Filtering framework at Twitter, which was used for applying custom filtering logic to Tweets, Users, and other entities, for health and product purposes.
